newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Telecom Eireann sees further fall in phone charges.
newsitem.headline: Telecom Eireann sees further fall in phone charges.

text.p: Ireland's Telecom Eireann on Monday welcomed a global trade agreement on telecommunications and said increased competition would lead to significant reductions in Irish telephone rates.
"Competition in telecoms will continue to force prices downward," Gerry O'Sullivan, head of corporate communications at Telcom Eireann, told Reuters.
Irish long distance telephone rates were likely to be cut by 50 percent over the next three years, he said.
Long distance rates have already fallen sharply in recent years with calls to Britain from Ireland now charged at 27 pence a minute compared with 60 pence three years ago.

The accord, signed by 68 countries at the World Trade Organisation in Geneva at the weekend, opens up most of the world's $600 billion telecommunications market and is expected to offer a major boost to the international economy.
"I think what we're seeing in the WTO is effectively governments throughout the world recognising the critical importance of telecoms as an underpinner of economic growth," O'Sullivan said.
He said the accord higlighted the importance of Telecom Eireann's strategic alliance with PTT Nederland and Sweden's Telia, which provides it with a link to AT & T Corp and Unisource.
"It links us to a global network which is very important from the point of view of servicing multinationals in particular," O'Sullivan said.
